svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Component · Blended clip row · on-picplace · wide
svg.desc: Mirrors App/BlendedClipRow.swift for a clip whose file is NOT on this device while PicPlace holds it (2026-09-26, plan §11 + §15 + §16): free up space removed it, or the project came down as a preview. model.blendFileMissing(blend) is true and PicPlace's list for the project names the file (PicPlaceController.blendAvailability == .onPicPlace — the row asks for the list itself as it shows a missing clip, askForListing, at most once a minute per project). The thumbnail is the blend's still (model.blendPosterURL — posters/<blend id>.jpg, which every records push carries since stage 3, drawn as an image, never graded again); it wears components/holdings-pill.blend.there.safe.svg at 0.8, 2 pt in (grey layers — on PicPlace, not here · the neutral ✓ — PicPlace holds it). The subtitle leads with where the clip is (BlendWhereLine): "On PicPlace · " + the plain subtitle. Where Open was, BlendDownloadButton's "Download" (12.5 pt semibold accent; "Downloading…", disabled, while the project's transfer runs — the pill's cloud turns to the amber ↓, holdings-pill.blend.downloading): it brings this blend alone down (downloadOriginals(kinds: [.blend], only: [its file])). A tap on the row asks first rather than opening a player with nothing in it (the parent's onPlay: ask(.blend(id), "Playing the clip") → .fetchPrompt). Same row, title and sample as blended-clip-row.default; the text column clipped 8 pt before Download's left edge (the README's clip rule — the code's own gap is 24 pt: HStack spacing 12 before the row's Spacer and 12 before the button), where SwiftUI truncates with an ellipsis.
